correctness.rationale: Direct Gram computation on the normalized curved hemisphere yields K(x,y)=1+3(x_h·y_h)+12(x3-1/2)(y3-1/2). For height z, conditional azimuth symmetry and convexity give F(sqrt(1-z²),z)<=F(1,z); convex interpolation bounds 0<z<=1/3 by an endpoint below L, and Cauchy-Schwarz bounds z>=1/3 by 2. An equatorial kernel has a negative cap entirely contained in the hemisphere, integrated exactly using the uniform spherical dot-product coordinate, yielding L=61 sqrt(5)/15-7>sqrt(13/3). This proves global uniqueness of equatorial maximizing rows. Triangle-equality and symmetry yield all L-infinity extremizers, L1 equality of norms and lack of L1 attainment. Standard-library checker replayed 96 supporting assertions; finite quadrature is not used as a proof.

value.rationale: Half-sphere affine least squares is the canonical degree-one projector on a simple bounded spherical patch; a sharp projector norm directly controls L-infinity approximation error and positivity undershoot. The closed form differs strictly from the full-sphere first-degree norm 5/3, and the global equator-only maximization plus distinction between L-infinity attainment and L1 nonattainment supply structural information not implied by general boundedness. Its fixed natural domain and exact extremizers make the precise invariant useful for stability benchmarks rather than a contrived numerical slice.
